chapter: Willie Lynch, the Blue Rhythm Band and Teddy Hill
title: Asking Irving Mills for more money and being fired
summary: On tour the band wanted more pay; at a meeting at Mills's office Holmes alone spoke up and was replaced, teaching him to speak only for himself.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: All right, we are now back with the Mills Blue Rhythm Band. And the band had apparently been out on tour...

Yeah, yeah, we was out on tour. And a lot of the smart boys got their heads together, because they was drawin' people into the dances, and they thought they were getting paid enough. So they got their heads together, and they're going to not strike, but they're going to ask for more money -- they want more money. So they asked me what I thought about it. "Fine if you get it. It's all right with me if you get it." But it's not my idea...
Well, apparently this got back to Mills even while you were on the road.
Well, everything we did got back to Mills. Everything that was said in the band got to Mills. You understand what I mean?
So anyway, he called the band back in off of the road...
Yeah. And we had a meeting at his office.

Yeah, down at 1500 Broadway or something -- the Brill Building or something like that, where he had his office. Wherever his office was at.

We go down, and he passes out the cigars and one thing or another, and he gives glad hands and so forth and so on. "Well, now, fellas, I hear there's a little trouble in the band. What seems to be the real problem? Now, let's have it. Let's have it out, talk it over, see what we can do about it."

It's very convenient. So we're all sittin' around. And I'm waiting for somebody to say somethin'. I was not an instigator of this idea. You know, I had no part of it. It was all right for me if they did, and if they didn't it was all right. Nobody said anything. I mean, we were sittin' around lookin' from one to the other. So I said, "Well, I'll start the ball rolling, then somebody else will pick me up." I just know somebody's going to pick me up. So I said, "Well, Mr. Mills, we decided with the crowd that we're getting on the road, that we're not making enough money, and we deserve a little bit more than what we're getting."

So he said, "Well, does anybody else have anything to

say?' And he looks around. And I look around. And you could hear a pin drop. He says, "Well, everybody else seems to be satisfied. All right. We will replace Holmes, and continue with the rest of the lists." He said, "We'll replace Holmes and continue with the rest of the (?)." So naturally, there was nothing for me to do but come out the band -- and I was out.
And no one else was fired. Just you.

Nobody said a word. They had no reason to get fired. Nobody said a word. And I don't think they got any more money either. They didn't ask for it! Not while I was there. Well, that taught me my biggest lesson in music: Speak for myself. Stay away from them ideas and them crowds and things.
